metadata.note_mistral: Mistral has only 50 tasks per combo (exploratory)

data_sources.accuracy: worker_data_audit_all_tables (verified against traces and paper tables)

primary_crossover.description: Selector topology shows opposite effects on different backbones
primary_crossover.interpretation: Strong models (Qwen) are topology-agnostic. Medium models (Gemma) benefit from selector's routing. Weak models (Llama) are harmed by selector's additional complexity.

crossover_analysis.difficulty_interaction_note: Difficulty stratification available only for round_robin topology. All backbones show monotonic accuracy decline with difficulty (easy > medium > hard). Gemma shows largest drop on hard tasks (89.1% → 65.7%, -23.4pp), suggesting potential for topology-difficulty interaction.

guidelines.recommendation: Any topology works; prefer round_robin or sequential for simplicity
guidelines.evidence: Qwen shows <0.4pp spread across topologies (89.7%–90.0%). No statistical difference.
guidelines.rationale: Strong models self-correct effectively regardless of communication structure. Simpler topologies save implementation complexity without accuracy cost.

guidelines.recommendation: Use selector topology for best accuracy
guidelines.evidence: Gemma selector achieves 83.0% vs 80.3% round_robin (+2.7pp). Selector's routing mechanism helps by directing messages to the most relevant agent.
guidelines.rationale: Models with moderate capability benefit from intelligent routing. The selector mechanism compensates for occasional reasoning failures by leveraging the stronger agent's output.

guidelines.evidence: Llama selector drops to 56.2% from 74.8% round_robin (-18.6pp). Sequential also degrades (71.6%).
guidelines.rationale: Selector mechanism adds meta-reasoning overhead that weak models cannot handle. Simple round_robin ensures all agents contribute equally, avoiding cascading failures from poor routing decisions.

guidelines.recommendation: Topology has no effect; focus on model capability first
guidelines.evidence: Mistral shows identical 52% accuracy across all topologies (n=50 each, exploratory).
guidelines.rationale: Below a capability threshold, multi-agent communication cannot compensate for fundamental reasoning limitations. Sample size is small (50 tasks).

guidelines.condition: Hard tasks (>4 reasoning steps) with any model
guidelines.recommendation: Consider that topology effects may be amplified on harder tasks
guidelines.evidence: Hard-task accuracy drops: Qwen 82.0%, Llama 66.3%, Gemma 65.7% (round_robin). Gemma's 23.4pp easy-hard gap suggests selector benefit may be concentrated on harder tasks.
guidelines.rationale: Difficulty stratification is from round_robin only. Cross-topology × difficulty interaction requires full stratified data across all topologies (available on server, not yet analyzed).
